method: Built-in image_gen, original generated illustrations, November 2026
ocean:
Create an ambitious flat magazine SPREAD illustration for fictional Horizons 1977 Tenerife, composed to weave around real typeset articles later. Landscape 22:17 ratio, request 3072x2368 resolution. No text or letters. Warm plain ivory paper ground. 1970s architectural illustration, hand-drawn ink and restrained flat petrol blue, ochre and sea green inks, fine printed stipple. NOT photoreal CGI.
Very specific composition: LEFT HALF the entire top 30 percent is empty ivory for a huge headline. Under that, at x=0–23% of whole spread from y=30–72%, keep an ivory column entirely empty for prose. A beautifully rounded yellow submarine passenger tram enters at x=35%, y=92%, bends upward through x=40%, y=62%, and disappears across the central gutter towards RIGHT. Its organic blue underwater surroundings and dark volcanic rock make an irregular diagonal border against the empty left text column. Tiny passengers, a cup shelf, a diver, undersea lamps. RIGHT HALF at y=5–58%: a large sectional-perspective of a SMALL underwater inhabited common room built against volcanic rock, warm amber windows, table, readers, coats and a towel, pragmatic access shaft visibly rising to the water surface. The room is submerged. Small fish ONLY in the water, no fish in sky. At the uppermost right distant Tenerife coastline with properly proportioned Teide ABOVE a clearly drawn waterline; treat as architectural cutaway not magical single perspective. RIGHT HALF bottom 33% is completely empty ivory, for two small article columns later. The whole art connects across gutter, but mostly a shaped cutout on ivory; absolutely no rectangular image frames. This should feel like entering an inhabited speculative world, with ordinary intimate lives inside extraordinary technology. No tropical coral reef. No dramatic digital lighting. No book mockup, fake folds, borders, headings, signatures or gibberish.
village:
Create a flat original magazine illustration on warm plain ivory for a fictional 1977 Tenerife proceedings. Landscape 22:17 ratio, request 3072x2368 resolution. No text anywhere. An irregular shaped CUTAWAY VILLAGE illustration, not a rectangular landscape: self-built modest white houses, tiny older cave rooms cut into dark volcanic coastal cliffs at Bocacangrejo. A long zigzag exterior staircase with landings traverses the whole composition from lower LEFT to upper RIGHT. It passes between small inhabited rooms: someone cooking, two neighbours handing a bowl through a window, an elderly person resting on a shaded step, laundry, a child, a fisherman repairing a net with another person quietly watching. A harbour glimpse and dark Atlantic bottom right; small distant Teide silhouette upper right, subordinate to the houses. There are no modern painted heart murals. 1970s illustrated field notebook: precise but lively ink, rough warm grey halftone collage texture, rusty red and muted olive spot colours, irregular edges dissolving to unprinted ivory. Tiny human activities supply the emotional centre.
Composition requirements for later real typesetting: upper LEFT quarter completely empty ivory. Lower LEFT quarter completely empty ivory. On the RIGHT HALF leave a large clean ivory cavity in the lower right corner about 28% of whole width and 30% of height; staircase travels along the top and left edge of this cavity. Buildings form a continuous diagonal band with irregular organic edges through the middle of the spread. No typography, labels, ruled diagram arrows, wireframes, blueprint, digital render, glossy photorealism, rounded infographic boxes, borders, mockup, fake crease. The architecture should physically make room for prose and be a walk for the reader's eye.
gathering: An original black-and-white halftone editorial illustration for an imaginary 1977 architecture conference on Tenerife. Request landscape 3072x2048. Four specific historical thinkers imagined at a working table in 1977: Paolo Soleri, Aldo Rossi with round spectacles, elderly Buckminster Fuller in spectacles, and sculptor Kenneth Snelson. Waist-up or seated, faces distinct with plausible age in 1977. They are not posing for the camera: Fuller and Snelson on the RIGHT carefully hold different parts of the same small tensegrity sculpture of THREE unconnected wooden struts supported by taut threads; the tension and their separate hands matter. Rossi LEFT studies a sketch of a square, Soleri at CENTRE-LEFT folds a densely built terraced-city paper model. Two unnamed women workshop participants also lean into the discussion at the far edges, active contributors with notebooks, not background servants. On the table a broad ragged-edge sheet with a freehand drawing of Tenerife's elongated island, mountainous contours and a recognizable Teide, varied tiny building proposals and a harbour. Coffee cups, pencil shavings, rolled paper; attentive, companionable disagreement. No readable writing, signatures or captions. Like a grainy 35mm documentary photograph reproduced as coarse black ink halftone, but presented as an illustrative reconstruction not a real recovered photo. Cut the figures and the table out against a completely plain warm ivory background; irregular silhouettes, no rectangular photo edge, no wall or room background. Concentrate people in the middle 70% of the image; generous plain ivory around all edges. Lively unposed gestures and real human proportions. No caricature, CGI, sepia tint, glossy lighting or present-day objects.
